617605e3-8c8f-4f69-a016-9e8d3cbed545.body: Development notes from my 1:1 with Elena. Private.

8759891b-7768-48b6-ad5f-4b401f19c0d8.title: Comp & hiring plan — 2026
8759891b-7768-48b6-ad5f-4b401f19c0d8.body: Roaster #2 hire and the FY26 comp bands. Private to leadership.

6d199dfc-dea1-4953-bbe1-621795b92adb.title: Newsletter idea — Solstice rotation
6d199dfc-dea1-4953-bbe1-621795b92adb.body: The seasonal Solstice release drives newsletter signups every quarter. Idea: let café accounts (The Nook) co-feature the rotation and cross-promote. Rosa picks the next single-origin; Tom confirms the farm lot.

e6384092-a43d-4db1-b606-b721ee6f5b01.title: Sunset Markets — save plan
e6384092-a43d-4db1-b606-b721ee6f5b01.body: Marcus is questioning our slot after soft dark-roast sell-through. Diagnosis: it's the SKU, not us. Swap Midnight Oak for Morning Ember 12oz, add an endcap promo for launch. Get him velocity numbers from Highland-comparable stores.

62ba47a7-9060-4b15-ab00-52718dffb07c.title: Roasting capacity is the constraint
62ba47a7-9060-4b15-ab00-52718dffb07c.body: Every big deal (Wildflower, Highland at scale) runs into the same wall: one roaster. Second roaster is the Q4 decision. Until then, don't sign volume we can't roast fresh — freshness is the whole brand.

f37897f8-5f41-4b15-afc7-a22784d88e60.title: Q3 pipeline review — notes
f37897f8-5f41-4b15-afc7-a22784d88e60.body: Two must-wins: Highland listing and the Sunset save. Wildflower is on hold until capacity. Cloudpeak renewal is easy — add the decaf upsell. Watch The Nook freshness expectations; keep roast-to-order tight.

4fd72b03-6ae2-4bcb-8d6a-573e0b53f757.title: Harbor private-label — profiles to sample
4fd72b03-6ae2-4bcb-8d6a-573e0b53f757.body: Sampling three house-blend profiles for Harbor this week: Midnight Oak as-is, a softer medium, and a chocolate-forward custom. Hassan wants their name on the bag. Nail the profile, then talk exclusivity and volume.

61bb2b2a-8084-4bba-bb7d-f878c513c693.title: Follow up with Grace — Highland projection
61bb2b2a-8084-4bba-bb7d-f878c513c693.body: Owe Grace the sell-through projection for the Morning Ember listing. Pull Riverbend's weekly velocity and scale to 12 stores. Attach the 90-day promo calendar. She decides slots next month — get it to her this week.

67f936d0-a506-4a4c-a286-1a4ea8edd584.title: Template: Wholesale pricing tiers
67f936d0-a506-4a4c-a286-1a4ea8edd584.body: Our wholesale tiers by weekly volume, with freight thresholds and the roast-to-order lead time baked in. Margin floors by segment (café, grocery, office, distributor). The distributor tier is deliberately thin — volume only, and only with roasting capacity to match.

39f360e0-e04d-4fe1-9fe8-2c961bc9c554.title: Account plan: Highland Grocery
39f360e0-e04d-4fe1-9fe8-2c961bc9c554.body: Goal: land the 12-store Morning Ember listing, then expand to a second SKU by Q4. Champion: Grace (category buyer), data-driven. Risks: shelf productivity scrutiny. Play: sell-through projection from Riverbend velocity + promo calendar + launch sampling. Expansion: add Evening Calm decaf once velocity is proven.

750417a6-8aed-4d42-a08c-bedd2fe0e5d3.title: Tasting note: Sunrise Light (new Yirgacheffe)
750417a6-8aed-4d42-a08c-bedd2fe0e5d3.body: New Yirgacheffe lot: jasmine on the nose, blueberry and lemon in the cup, tea-like body. Bright but not sharp. Slightly higher acidity than last lot — flag for the pour-over accounts who love it, may be much for milk drinks.

2a28f710-4b1f-42f7-84d9-e15731b074e6.title: Tasting note: Morning Ember (current lot)
2a28f710-4b1f-42f7-84d9-e15731b074e6.body: Current Huila lot: milk chocolate up front, orange zest in the middle, clean nutty finish. Sweet through the cool-down. Roasted to the first-crack-plus profile. Consistent with the flagship spec — approved for wholesale.

63a88d18-98d7-4f3a-a3f3-de8a4d081bd6.title: Playbook: Account save
63a88d18-98d7-4f3a-a3f3-de8a4d081bd6.body: When an account goes at-risk (soft sell-through, a quiet buyer): diagnose the SKU, not the relationship. Usually one product is dragging. Propose a swap to a proven blend, add a launch promo, and put a roast date on every bag. Save the slot before you defend the price.

077983f7-682c-47f0-a729-f298213f9a09.title: Playbook: Winning a grocery shelf listing
077983f7-682c-47f0-a729-f298213f9a09.body: How we win (and keep) a grocery slot: lead with sell-through data from a comparable account, bring a 90-day promo calendar, offer in-store sampling for launch, and never open with a discount. The buyer is protecting shelf productivity — give them the numbers, not the price.

8e51f41c-118a-412d-b33a-28d084c6107d.title: Drop the downtown café at their price
8e51f41c-118a-412d-b33a-28d084c6107d.body: They wanted our price to match a regional bulk roaster. Drop it. We don't win on price — we win on roast-to-order freshness and the story. Chasing that account would train the market to expect discounts.

0e73753d-1ebc-40a5-ba54-0fa6e714588c.title: Go on Highland private-label marketing plan
0e73753d-1ebc-40a5-ba54-0fa6e714588c.body: Grace won't give up a slot for a price alone. Go: build the sell-through projection from Riverbend's velocity, add a 90-day promo calendar and in-store sampling. Win it on the plan, protect the margin.

4863dc76-7b4a-4d22-9630-5fef74b2d67b.title: Hold on the Wildflower distribution deal
4863dc76-7b4a-4d22-9630-5fef74b2d67b.body: Tempting top-line, but 40 cafés at once would blow past our roasting capacity and the margin is thin. Decision: hold until we've added the second roaster in Q4. Revisit with capacity in hand — don't win volume we can't roast fresh.

e8bf1610-970a-4e78-b57e-5302178fee65.title: Metro Roasters — lost
e8bf1610-970a-4e78-b57e-5302178fee65.body: Lost a downtown café to a cheaper regional roaster last quarter. They chose price over freshness. Lesson: we don't win on price, we win on roast-to-order and story.
